fields.description: Address tenants use to reach this Suite Cloud, e.g. https://cloud.frappemail.com. Leave blank to use this site's own URL. Hosted sites are given it to call Suite Cloud, so it must be reachable from Frappe Cloud: on a development machine, set a tunnel's address.
fields.label: Public URL

fields.description: Take a tenant's word for its domains: add them without the TXT record that proves control, and treat them as verified without checking their DNS records. For a development cloud, whose test domains exist in no public DNS. Never on a shared cluster: a wrongly claimed domain locks its owner out, and Stalwart accepts mail for every domain marked verified. Turning it off re-checks the domains it vouched for.
fields.label: Skip Domain Verification

fields.description: How long an install, bootstrap or upgrade job may run before it is marked failed. Bootstrapping the first node includes waiting for a certificate, so keep this generous. 1800 = 30 minutes.
fields.label: Server Job Timeout (Seconds)

fields.description: How long fetched DMARC reports are kept. Stalwart drops its own copy after 30 days, so this is the only history a tenant sees.
fields.label: DMARC Report Retention (Days)

fields.description: How long fetched TLS reports are kept. Stalwart drops its own copy after 30 days, so this is the only history a tenant sees.
fields.label: TLS Report Retention (Days)
Tenant Email
fields.description: Sites connected to Suite Cloud send their mail through it, e.g. invites and password resets.
The outgoing Email Account each tenant type's sites send through. A site whose type has none cannot send mail.
fields.label: Email Accounts

fields.description: Send under the tenant's title, e.g. Acme <noreply@example.com>. Off: under the Email Account's name.
fields.label: Use Tenant Title as Sender Name

fields.description: The agents on Stalwart and SFU nodes push logs and metrics to the telemetry API; the loader copies them into Insights.
fields.label: Telemetry

fields.description: Runs the Suite Cloud Agent on every Stalwart node and egress gateway and opens the telemetry API to them. Each Agent signs in with its cluster's Agent Key and Agent Secret. Turning this on or off queues an Install Agent job on every server that runs an Agent: off, the job stops the Agent.
fields.label: Enable Telemetry

fields.description: How long events and metrics are kept in Insights. Older rows are deleted daily.
fields.label: Telemetry Retention (Days)

fields.description: How many requests one node may send per minute, counted by its address.
fields.label: Telemetry Requests per Minute

fields.description: How many records one request may hold. Larger batches mean fewer requests; each is validated whole.
fields.label: Telemetry Records per Request

fields.description: Every five minutes, a Telemetry Alert is opened for a node that stopped reporting or logs too many errors, and resolved when the condition clears.
fields.label: Telemetry Alerts

fields.description: Email addresses to notify when an alert opens or resolves, separated by commas or lines. Empty: alerts are recorded but nobody is mailed.
fields.label: Telemetry Alert Recipients

fields.description: A node that reported in the last day but sent nothing for this long is a Silent Host.
fields.label: Silent Host After (Minutes)

fields.description: A node whose error-level events exceed this share of its events in the last hour (at least 100 events) has an Error Rate alert.
fields.label: Error Rate Alert (%)

fields.description: The Suite Cloud Agent runs on every Stalwart node and egress gateway and ships the Stalwart log and host metrics to the telemetry API. Provisioning installs it when Enable Telemetry is on and a build exists.
fields.label: Agent

fields.description: How often the agent retries a batch after a server or network failure before it skips the batch. Rate limits never count.
fields.label: Agent Max Attempts

fields.description: How often the agent samples the machine and Stalwart's metrics.
fields.label: Metrics Interval (Seconds)

fields.description: On a node that already holds log files, ship them too the first time the agent starts there. Off: only new lines are shipped.
fields.label: Ship Existing Logs

fields.description: The agent deletes a rotated log file this many days after it was shipped whole. 0: never. The node's tmpfiles rule removes log files after 14 days in any case.
fields.label: Delete Shipped Logs After (Days)

fields.description: The agent version Build Agent last built on this bench host; what provisioning installs.
fields.label: Built Agent Version

fields.description: Stalwart release that new clusters install, e.g. v0.16.20. Existing clusters keep their own version until you run Upgrade Nodes on them.
fields.label: Stalwart Version

fields.description: Where the node downloads the Stalwart archive from. {version} is replaced with the release and {target} with the platform, e.g. x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.
fields.label: Stalwart Download URL Template

fields.description: Release of Stalwart's spam filter rules a cluster imports on its first start, e.g. v3.0.1. Newer rules can use expression functions an older server lacks, so change it together with the Stalwart Version. Empty imports the latest release.
fields.label: Spam Filter Rules Version

fields.description: Release of stalwart-cli installed next to the server, e.g. v1.0.12. Only used on a node while it bootstraps a cluster.
fields.label: Stalwart CLI Version

fields.description: Where the node downloads the stalwart-cli archive from. Same placeholders as the server URL, but {target} is the static build, e.g. x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.
fields.label: Stalwart CLI Download URL Template

fields.description: Verify the TLS certificate of clusters and egress gateways when talking to their management API. Turn off only on a development site whose cluster has a staging certificate.
fields.label: Verify Stalwart TLS Certificates

fields.description: Every domain gets an RSA key (selector frappemail-rsa); check this to add an Ed25519 key as well (selector frappemail-ed25519). Off by default because many receivers still ignore Ed25519 signatures and treat the mail as unsigned. Keys are generated and held by the cluster and never rotate. Applies to domains registered on Stalwart after the change, the cluster default domain included; existing domains keep the keys they were created with.
fields.label: Sign with Ed25519 as well as RSA

fields.description: Certificate authority clusters request their TLS certificates from. While testing use https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory to avoid rate limits; staging certificates are not trusted by mail clients.
fields.label: ACME Directory URL

fields.description: Address the certificate authority writes to about expiring certificates. Used by clusters that do not set their own contact.
fields.label: ACME Contact Email

fields.description: How long resolvers may cache the records Suite Cloud publishes, used when a DNS Zone sets no TTL of its own. Also suggested to tenants for their domain records. 300 keeps node changes quick to roll out.
fields.label: Default DNS TTL (Seconds)

fields.description: Address of Frappe Cloud's control plane, e.g. https://central.frappe.cloud. Suite Cloud creates its servers there.
fields.label: Central URL

fields.description: The team that owns Suite Cloud's servers, picked from the teams the API key's user belongs to; enter the URL, key and secret first. The key's user needs a team-wide role with server:create, server:view, cluster:view and server:console in it.
fields.label: Central Team

fields.description: Where a tenant's site goes when its signup names no region. Only enabled regions are offered: run Sync Regions under Frappe Cloud, then enable a region and set its proxy zone.
fields.label: Default Region

fields.description: Central image offering new servers boot from; its newest image without a baked site is used.
fields.label: Image Offering

fields.description: Central plan of new servers. Blank takes the first plan Central offers in the region.
fields.label: Plan

fields.description: The most sites any server takes, Suite sites and others together, whatever its size. Each server's Max Sites is worked out from its memory and disk below and never exceeds this.
fields.label: Max Sites per Server

fields.description: With Create Servers Automatically on, a region with fewer free slots than this gets one more server, at most one per hour.
fields.label: Minimum Free Site Slots

fields.description: Add a server to a region that runs short of free site slots. Each server is billed to the Central team.
fields.label: Create Servers Automatically

fields.description: A server takes as many sites as both its memory and its disk allow, after what the server itself needs: (memory − reserved) ÷ memory per site, and the same for disk. Recalculated whenever Central reports the server's size, so a resize on the dashboard counts.
fields.label: Server Sizing

fields.description: Memory the bench needs before any site: Frappe, the Suite app, MariaDB, Redis and the workers.
fields.label: Memory Reserved for the Server (MB)

fields.description: Disk the system, the bench and its apps take before any site.
fields.label: Disk Reserved for the Server (GB)

fields.description: Git repository of the Suite app each server installs.
fields.label: Repository

fields.description: What new servers install. Servers already set up keep the commit they installed.
fields.label: Branch or Tag

fields.description: Sites with Suite installed kept waiting in each enabled region, so a signup gets one at once. 0 creates every site on demand.
fields.label: Ready Sites per Region

fields.description: Accept signups through the public signup API. Each one creates a tenant and claims a site.
fields.label: Allow Signup

fields.description: Accept a signup email with a +tag, e.g. john+test@example.com. Off, such an email is refused: every tag of one mailbox could sign up again. On, the owner's account on the site leaves the tag out, e.g. john@acme.example.com.
fields.label: Allow Sub-addressed Emails at Signup

fields.description: Zone under which each site gets its label as its primary domain, e.g. acme.example.app. It may be the tenant mail zone: site domains then go under sites, e.g. acme.sites.example.com beside the mail domain acme.example.com. It needs a DNS provider.
fields.label: Site DNS Zone

fields.description: Zone under which each tenant gets its label as its mail domain, e.g. acme.example.com. Every hosted site gets one, so it is required once Central is set. It may be the site DNS zone. It needs a DNS provider and must not be the zone of a Stalwart cluster.
fields.label: Tenant Mail Zone
